title: Progress with a model that does not call tools
request: In the live check, a small local model answered the Home conversation in prose and never called a tool, so nothing was recorded and the chat stopped. Make the conversation keep moving whatever the model does: the user must always have a next step.
spec: In HomeAgent.model_turn, when a turn ends with no tool call and a question is pending, record the user's reply as that question's answer in code; when no question is pending and something is still unknown, ask the next scripted question after the model's text. Done when a scripted model that never calls a tool still leads to a recorded outcome, moment and action, and a summary.
plan: Run the Home conversation against the local Ollama model (qwen2.5-coder:1.5b) after the OpenAI account refused every request for lack of credit, and see where it stalls.
Pull the 'record the answer, mark the question answered, redraw the workflow, ask the next thing' block out of script_turn into one take_answer method, so the script and the model path share it.

In model_turn, remember the open question before the model speaks and whether any tool ran; when none ran, answer the still-open question from the user's text in code, start a simulation if the user asked for one and no data exists, or otherwise ask the next scripted question.
Write a test with a scripted client that only ever returns text, and run the draft-flow tests.

decisions.decision: Code, not the model, takes the answer when the model calls no tool.
decisions.why: The answer to the pending question is the user's own message; recording it needs no model judgment, and a small model that only talks must not be able to stall the product.

decisions.decision: The fallback only answers a question that is still open after the model's turn.
decisions.why: A model that did call record or ask_user in that turn has already moved the conversation; answering again would record the same text twice or skip a question.

decisions.decision: Reuse one take_answer method for the script and for the fallback.
decisions.why: Two copies of 'record, mark answered, redraw, ask next' would drift apart; one method keeps the scripted and model paths identical.

change: dclab_rnd/draft/chat.py: take_answer(draft_id, q, value) extracted from script_turn; reply passes the user's text into model_turn; model_turn notes the open question and whether a tool ran, and after a tool-less turn records the answer, starts a requested simulation, or asks the next question. tests/test_draft_flow.py gains test_a_model_that_only_talks_does_not_stall_the_conversation and an updated streaming test.

findings.defect: With a model that never calls a tool, the Home conversation stopped: nothing was recorded and no next question came.
findings.scenario: Live check with qwen2.5-coder:1.5b on the local machine: the user answers the outcome question; the model replies with friendly prose and no record or ask_user call; the draft's understanding stays empty and the chat waits for ever.
findings.cause: model_turn assumed the model would drive the conversation through tools and had no path for a turn with no tool call.
findings.fix: After a turn with no tool call, code records the reply as the answer to the question that is still open (or starts a requested simulation, or asks the next question), as the script would.
findings.test: test_a_model_that_only_talks_does_not_stall_the_conversation: a Talker client that always returns text; after four answers the outcome, moment and action are recorded and the last message is the summary.

findings.defect: The streaming test failed after the change: the streamed tokens no longer belonged to the last message.
findings.scenario: test_streaming_client_sends_token_chunks_then_the_message_replaces_them compared the token events with the draft's last message; now the next question follows the model's text, so the last message is the question, not the streamed reply.
findings.cause: The test assumed the model's text is always the final message of a turn.
findings.fix: The test looks up the streamed message by its id instead of taking the last message.

outcome: Done and pushed: a model that only talks no longer stalls Home; the code records the answer and asks the next question. make rd-check passed (320 tests) and the four end-to-end flows passed.
lessons: A live run with a small local model finds failure modes a scripted client never shows; script the failure afterwards so it stays tested.
Every agent turn needs a deterministic next step when the model does nothing useful.
When a fix inserts a message, re-check tests that assume message order.
